answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF: a long chain of modular squarings where each result depends on the previous one. GPUs may run separate chains in parallel, but cannot divide one chain to eliminate its sequential delay; simulating many clones therefore requires proportionally more hardware and time. The spiral of dependent steps is the bottleneck, while quartz and mesa serve as distinct verification labels, not shortcuts.
